ruling_on_the_failure:
WHAT IT IS. A false positive in U3c's test-only held-bound check (G-NC2, Conn::check_held_bound, crates/net/src/l2/delay.rs:528-543). It depends on timing. Nothing shows a defect in DelayStream itself. I found the cause by reading the code; I ran nothing, so the cause is not yet confirmed by a run.

THE EVIDENCE.
(1) What the check samples. It reads held = bytes[d].len(): all the down plaintext that S has not taken yet, including records already released. It compares that with 64 KB plus the acknowledged prefix of recs[d].get(released[d]), which is the front record NOT yet released.
(2) A release changes the bound but not held. A release (harvest, delay.rs:675-686) moves the front record into released and leaves held unchanged. If that record carried the prefix that put held above 64 KB, the bound drops by that prefix at the release while held stays where it was. This lasts until the pump writes the record into S (delay.rs:1727-1761).
(3) The pump samples in exactly that state. Its up loop steps the model to a fresh now on every pass, after the down loop (delay.rs:1813-1814). Its closing block then calls held_now() (delay.rs:1879). The code's own R1 comment (:1868-1872, also :1800) says a down record released there "is still unwritten here".
(4) Real time decides it. The window is the pump's real-time down-loop span, or another task's step while the lock is free (the test loop calls ds.snapshot() -> current() every iteration). It is therefore wider under load.
(5) No extra byte was ever admitted. Held grows only at poll_write (the one extend, delay.rs:1574). At each write, down_free = free_budget - released_model (delay.rs:473-477), so held <= 64 KB + the prefix at that write. Between writes held only falls. The bound therefore holds everywhere held can grow. The test's second assert also held: excess 14,326 B < 16,406.
(6) Why only the bites build. Its npt-net library has 169 tests: the two WebTransport features add QUIC-at-P2 sessions that run beside this test. The measured build has 160. The same test passed in the measured build of the same run (test.log:510).
(7) The log line, for the record: "samples above the bound [1, 0]". In delay.rs, DOWN = 0 (:121), so this is one down sample.

IS IT THIS LANE'S? No, by every route I could find.
- I checked `git diff --stat 044fab1 561bf42 -- spikes/netcode-proof/crates/net`: it prints nothing.
- npt-net does depend on npt-l1 (crates/net/Cargo.toml:19-20, for Profile). But the lane's npt-l1 change is +33 -0 and only adds: a new struct DatagramCounts and a read-only method FateLog::server_datagrams_since. Nothing outside l1 and lab calls them (grep). Profile, ReorderStep and P2 are untouched.
- No Cargo.toml or Cargo.lock changed.
- The lane's SERIES.md bytes do reach the npt-net binary, through include_str! in three other test modules (names.rs:143, delay_names.rs:449, socket_tests.rs:390). Those tests passed, and the failing test reads no file.
- cargo runs test binaries one at a time, so the lane's new tests never ran beside this one.
- The shared target was locked exclusively, and the log's "other cargo or rustc now" line is empty.
- npt-lab does not depend on npt-net at all (crates/lab/Cargo.toml). DelayStream is therefore outside every C62H-BOUND evidence path: lab, l1, judge and the L1 sets.
- I checked the grep counts myself: FAILED appears only in failed-steps/test.log; "... ok" appears in 96 logs.

SEVERITY.
- Medium, on U3c's code: a real defect in a test-only check that can fail on correct behaviour. The workaround is a counted re-run under a stated rule. It stops a counted check.mjs run about 1 time in 97, and never yields a wrong PASS.
- No finding against C62H-BOUND.
- One more Low: check.mjs's bites build runs without --no-fail-fast, so this one failure hid 202 of the 632 bites tests (430 ran). The crates that did not run are npt-proto, room, server, sim, super and tcpinfo. The lane's crates (judge, l1, lab) all ran and passed.
